title: Universal Responds After All 3 Hours of The Odyssey Leak on Social Media
summary: Universal moved quickly to remove unauthorized uploads after a high-quality, full 2 hour 53 minute copy of Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey was posted to X/Twitter and viewed millions of times. Variety reported more than 2.1 million views before takedowns. Universal said it initiated takedown protocols and will pursue remedies. The leak is unlikely to dent the film's strong box office, and the incident sparked reactions about streaming, piracy and AI recreations.
content:
Universal has stepped in after a high-quality upload of Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey leaked on X/Twitter. While many headed to theaters to catch the Greek epic on its second weekend, thousands instead watched an astonishingly high-quality — though inferior — version of the film from the comfort of their homes or on their phones. The film's runtime, roughly two hours and 53 minutes, was seen in full on the platform.

Most, if not all, uploads across X were removed in one way or another, with the most popular post taken down entirely. Responses to the leak remained, showing a mix of surprise, amusement and criticism from users. Some joked about watching the three-hour movie in a tiny subscreen while scrolling their timelines; others reported the video being removed the moment they started watching.

As reported by Variety, the leaked post had garnered more than 2.1 million views by the time Universal was able to take it down. Universal told the outlet that "We became aware of the unauthorized posting of the film and immediately initiated takedown protocols. We take copyright infringement seriously and will pursue all appropriate remedies to protect our content and intellectual property rights." The company said it would pursue all appropriate legal and technical responses.

Industry observers say the leak is unlikely to meaningfully slow the film's commercial momentum. The Odyssey opened to a career-best global debut for Nolan, with an opening weekend total of $264.1 million and continued strong performance in its second weekend. Studios and distributors often face this type of piracy risk with high-profile releases, but box office demand for premium formats can remain intact.

The story also stoked discussion about AI and recreations: X overseer Elon Musk said his AI tool Grok could produce its own version of The Odyssey before the end of 2026, claiming that such an AI-generated retelling would be "historically accurate and true to the art of Homer." The comment fed broader conversation about AI-generated content and how it intersects with intellectual property and creative attribution.

Nolan famously shot The Odyssey entirely using IMAX cameras, making unauthorized digital copies particularly disappointing for the filmmaker and exhibitors who emphasize premium large-format presentation. IMAX CEO Richard Gelfond has said building more 70mm IMAX projectors is "not practical," highlighting industry constraints in meeting demand for the director's preferred exhibition format.

Michael Cripe, a freelance writer with IGN, reported on the incident and its aftermath. The leak and the resulting social-media chatter underscore ongoing tensions between studios, platforms and audiences over access, piracy, and the shifting economics of theatrical windows and online distribution.

Related reads referenced in coverage note The Odyssey's box office durability, with a reported second-weekend global haul reinforcing the film's commercial strength despite the unauthorized upload.
